summary: CKGSB's global marketing is pivoting to prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China for search/AI visibility while executing a busy autumn event and content calendar, with immediate attention needed on the Outlook lockout and several time-sensitive approvals.
summaryDetail: The top priority is the global marketing strategy shift: Asia Star and Intelligent China are now the lead programs for search/AI visibility, with US partner programs (including Berkeley as a possible third) on hold pending the audit. This week, the team must resolve the Outlook account lockout by updating passwords across all devices and confirming the backend unlock with JSB, and Julie needs Prof. Erica Li's approval to publish the Q3 2026 Business Sentiment Index. Event and content work is ramping up: Graeme will share updated registration figures for the Nov 13 European Chamber Shanghai event, Amber must provide Ms. Singh's bio and headshot for the Women in Leadership Forum, and Ira and Kaylee need to review the warm-up video script before Moreaid edits. Upcoming items include the knowledge website redesign working session (Joseph, Julie, team lead) to finalize menu categorization and article templates, and Joseph's return to discuss Flow's 2026 report and the website/SEM contract renewal with Gontran. The team also approved the Sino-Swiss Economic Forum cooperation report email and finalized the global marcom work report for leadership submission.
